question: Sheikh,  I always forget how many sujud i made,whatt should I do?
title: Sheikh,  I always forget how many sujud i made,whatt should I do?
answer:
Assalamu alaikum wa rehmatAllah,
If this is a recurring problem in every salah, you need to work on developing khushoo (focus and attention) in your salah. If you are not certain, assume you didn’t perform it and do it and then offer two prostration s of sahu after Salam.

question: Assalamu alaikum, is it allowed to cross in front of a person that is praying?
title: Assalamu alaikum, is it allowed to cross in front of a person that is praying?
answer:
You should note – may Allaah forgive you – that you have committed a great sin, which is speaking about Allaah without knowledge. This is a sin which Allaah mentioned in conjunction with shirk. Allaah says (interpretation of the meaning):   “Say (O Muhammad): (But) the things that my Lord has indeed forbidden are Al-Fawaahish (great evil sins and every kind of unlawful sexual intercourse) whether committed openly or secretly, sins (of all kinds), unrighteous oppression, joining partners (in worship) with Allaah for which He has given no authority, and saying things about Allaah of which you have no knowledge” [al-A’raaf 7:33]
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “Whoever introduces a good way in Islam which is followed after he dies will have a reward like that of those who did it, without that detracting from their reward in the slightest. Whoever introduces a bad way in Islam which is followed after he dies will have a burden of sin like that of those who did it, without that detracting from their burden in the slightest.” (Narrated by Muslim, 1017, from Jareer ibn ‘Abd-Allaah).
So you have to repent to Allaah and seek His forgiveness for this sin. I ask Allaah to bless you with sincere repentance.
You should also strive to put right your mistake by telling those who heard what you said before without knowledge.
With regard to the question that you mention, if someone wants to pass in front of a person who is praying, one of the following scenarios must apply:
1 – If he passes in front of the one who is praying, i.e., in the area between the spot where he puts his forehead when he prostrates and where he stands, this is haraam, and indeed it is a major sin as the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “If the one who passes in front of a person who is praying knew what (a burden of sin) he bears, it would be better for him to stand for forty rather than pass in front of him.” Abu’l-Nadar – one of the narrators –

question: A woman was bedridden for about 4-5 days in ramadhan and during this time she did not pray nor did she fast.Later (after ramadhan) on she had the operation and did not pray for about a week.Now what can she do for these fasts and salah?

answer:
As for the prayers, she was wrong for not praying them if she was able to pray but didn’t! She can’t make up for what was abandoned intentionally.
As for fasting, she must make them up.

question: It is not permissible to pray in tight clothes. But can one pray in clothes which are loose enough but gets stretched and tight whenever one bows and prostrates?
title: It is not permissible to pray in tight clothes. But can one pray in clothes which are loose enough but gets stretched and tight whenever one bows and prostrates?
answer:
This should be avoided!
The clothing that is prescribed for women to pray in is any clothing that covers her entire body apart from the face and hands; it should be loose and opaque, so that it does not show the shape of any part of her body.
The fact that a woman’s clothing should cover all of her body whilst praying is indicated by the hadeeth of Umm Salamah (may Allaah be pleased with her) who was asked about what clothes a woman should pray in. she said: “She should pray in a khimaar (head cover) and a long chemise that covers the tops of her feet.” Narrated by Abu Dawood, 639. It was also narrated in a marfoo’ report (i.e., attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him)). Al-Haafiz ibn Hajar said in Buloogh al-Maraam (p. 40): The imams classed the mawqoof report as saheeh. Ibn Taymiyah said: The well known view is that it is mawqoof, with an isnaad that stops at Umm Salamah, but it carries the same weight as a marfoo’ report. Sharh Kitaab al-Salaah min al-‘Umdah, p. 365.
And the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “Allaah does not accept the prayer of a woman who menstruates (i.e., an adult woman) unless her head is covered.” Narrated by Abu Dawood, 641; al-Tirmidhi, 377; Ibn Maajah, 655; classed as saheeh by al-Albaani in Saheeh al-Jaami’, 7747.
So it is essential to wear something that covers the entire body apart from the face. The scholars differed as to whether it is obligatory for a woman to cover her hands and feet when praying.
With regard to the hands: the majority of scholars are of the view that it is not obligatory to cover them. Two views were narrated concerning that from Imam Ahmad. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyah was of the view that it is not obligatory. It says in al-Insaaf: That is the correct view.
With regard to the feet: the majority of Maalikis, Shaafa’is and Hanbalis are of the view that it is obligatory to cover them. This is also the view stated in a fatwa of the Standing Committee for

question: In salah how do you position your feet when sitting in the first tashahudd and in the second tashahudd when you pray 3 or 4 rakats?
title: In salah how do you position your feet when sitting in the first tashahudd and in the second tashahudd when you pray 3 or 4 rakats?
answer:
For the first tashahud you sit in iftiraash (Iftiraash means sitting on the left thigh with the right foot upwards and its toes pointed towards the qiblah)
For the final tashahud you sit in tawarruk (can be done in 2 ways: 1 – The left foot is laid down and the right foot is held upright, and both are held out to the right, with the buttocks on the ground. 2 – Both feet are laid down and held out to the right side, and the buttocks are on the ground. )

question: Sujood As Sahu (Prostrations of Forgetfulness)
title: Sujood As Sahu (Prostrations of Forgetfulness)
answer:
Question: Can you explain the Sujood of as-Sahu? When do they have to be done after the Tasleem (the Salaam)and when do they have to be done before?
Answer: Sujood as-Sahu (the Prostrations of Forgetfulness) are either performed before Salaam or after Salaam (if you do it after Salaam, then you have to offer another Salaam after the prostrations). Sheikh Muhammad ibn Salih ibn Uthaimeen, may Allah have mercy on his soul, classified this and divided it.
However, before that, we have to know that there are three types of sayings and actions in the prayer: The Pillars, The Mandatory things and The Things that are Sunnah.
1) Examples of the Pillars include reciting Surat al-Fatiha, the standing position, offering Ruku’, offering Sujood, etc. If one forgets a pillar and doesn’t offer it, his prayer is void and must pray again. But if he remembers and offers it while in prayer, his prayer is valid.
2) Examples of the Mandatory things include: the first Tashahhud, if it is a 3 or 4 Rak’ah prayer, saying ‘Subhana Rabbiyal ‘Azeem’ in Ruku’, saying ‘Subhana Rabbiyal Aa’la’ in Sujood, the Takbeers (saying ‘Allahu Akbar’) When moving from one position to another between pillars and saying ‘Sami’ Allahu liman Hamidah’ when rising from Ruku’, etc. If He leaves a mandatory act deliberately, his prayer is void. If he does it out of forgetfulness, he must prostrate for that{Sujood As Sahu}
3) Examples of the Sunan (plural of Sunnah) include: raising the hands when saying Allahu Akbar and Sami’ Allahu liman Hamidah, putting the right palm over the left on the chest, etc. These things are Sunnah; meaning, even if you don’t do them, your prayer is still valid.
Now, there are 4 cases when you have to offer Sujood as-Sahu:
1) Concerning the mandatory things, if you make a mistake in them (such as saying by mistake, ‘Subhaana Rabbiyal A’ala in Ruku’ instead of ‘Subhaana Rabbiyal ‘Azeem’) or forget any of them (such as forgetting to say ‘Allahu Akbar’ when moving from pillar to pi

question: Kindly help me out with prostration of forgetfulness in writing as the one uploaded on you tube has a voice which is quite unclear so unable to understand with clarity. kindly provide with the knowledge sheik
title: Kindly help me out with prostration of forgetfulness in writing as the one uploaded on you tube has a voice which is quite unclear so unable to understand with clarity. kindly provide with the knowledge sheik
answer:
Praise be to Allaah.
Shaykh Muhammad al-‘Uthaymeen was asked this question and said:
The correct view is that this does not invalidate your prayer, because doubts often come to a man without him wanting them to. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) explained the ruling concerning doubts in prayer, and that doubts fall into two categories:
1 – When the person doubts the number of rak’ahs he has prayed, but he thinks one of the two is more likely. In this case he should act upon what he is more certain of, and complete the prayer on that basis, then say the salaam and do the prostration of forgetfulness (sajdat al-sahw) after the salaam.
2 – When he doubts the number of rak’ahs, and neither number seems more likely to him. In this case he should act upon the lower number, because that is more certain and the higher number is doubtful, and he should complete the prayer based on the lower number, then do two prostrations for forgetfulness before the salaam. His prayer will not be invalidated in that case.

question: Suppose an Imam finishes the second prostration of the fourth rakah in Thuhr prayer and he mistakenly starts going to the standing position; but before he can do so, the congregation reminds him (by saying ‘SubhanAllaah’); he then sits down for the tashahudd. title: Suppose an Imam finishes the second prostration of the fourth rakah in Thuhr prayer and he mistakenly starts going to the standing position; but before he can do so, the congregation reminds him (by saying ‘SubhanAllaah’); he then sits down for the tashahudd. Are the two prostration of forgetfulness  a must in this case?

If he stood up or was half way, he has to offer sujood assahu. But if he didn’t stand up but was almost to do so, he doesn’t need to prostrate for forgetfulness.

question: I’m trying to perfect my salah. I understand the different movements and to take my time, but I don’t understand what I should visualise during salah. What image should I see when I am praying? I know the hadith of the Prophet Muhammad Peace be upon him when he said to pray as you see Allah or as Allah sees you. But what do I see? Allah as light?
title: I’m trying to perfect my salah. I understand the different movements and to take my time, but I don’t understand what I should visualise during salah. What image should I see when I am praying? I know the hadith of the Prophet Muhammad Peace be upon him when he said to pray as you see Allah or as Allah sees you. But what do I see? Allah as light?
answer:
The hadeeth doesn’t say pray as if you see Allah but rather worship Allah as if you can see Him! There is no visualizing here but rather the knowledge of Allah’s watching over you and worshiping Him as if you can see Him, though no one can see Him in this life but the impact of that is overwhelming on the Muslim.

Is this sunnah?
title: I was at Jummah congregation yesterday and saw a man next to me whom during the sujud in the first rakah decided to sit for like 3 seconds and said Allahu Akbar while sitting for like 3 secs with raising his hands while saying the takbeer while still sitting down when all of us have stood up including the imam has even started reciting Fatiha for the second rakah. Is this sunnah?
answer:
There is what is known as jalastul istiraha which is a sunnah. This is to sit for few seconds after the second prostration before standing to the second or fourth Rakah. This is a sunnah and the Prophet salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam used to do it. However, there is no raising of the hands in it.

question: At time of isha prayer, dinner is served, but a person or two is not hungry and wants to pray first, also the wife wants to come along with the husband to the masjid. Is it correct if they pray first then come and eat or was it wrong for them to leave dinner which served and go pray, also if the wife wants to come to the masjid with the husband, can she be refused to come to the masjid?
title: At time of isha prayer, dinner is served, but a person or two is not hungry and wants to pray first, also the wife wants to come along with the husband to the masjid. Is it correct if they pray first then come and eat or was it wrong for them to leave dinner which served and go pray, also if the wife wants to come to the masjid with the husband, can she be refused to come to the masjid?
answer:
If he is not hungry or eager to eat, he should go to the masjid first! As for the woman, it is best for her to pray home but if she wants to go, this is permissible and he should not prevent her unless there is a valid excuse!

question: During the prayer, can I recite Quran by looking in it? (By holding or keeping in front)
title: During the prayer, can I recite Quran by looking in it? (By holding or keeping in front)
answer:
There is nothing wrong with reading Qur’aan from the Mus-haf during a naafil prayer, such as qiyaam al-layl.
But in the case of obligatory prayers, it is makrooh to do that, because in most cases there is no need for it. But if there is a need, then there is nothing wrong with reading from the Mus-haf in that case.

question: If a muslim does various kinds of good deeds, always help people but do not perform salaat, then will he get the reward for his good deeds?
title: If a muslim does various kinds of good deeds, always help people but do not perform salaat, then will he get the reward for his good deeds?
answer:
If he does not pray at all, he is not a muslim. The health and wealth he is in is his reward for his good deeds.
 
Praise be to Allaah.
 
Negligence in performing prayers is a great sin, and a sign of extreme negligence, because prayer  is the most important pillar of Islam after the Shahaadatayn (twin testimony of faith). Allaah warns those who take the matter of prayer lightly and do not pray on time, as He says (interpretation of the meaning):
“Then, there has succeeded them a posterity who have given up As-Salaat (the prayers) [i.e. made their Salaat (prayers) to be lost, either by not offering them or by not offering them perfectly or by not offering them in their proper fixed times] and have followed lusts. So they will be thrown in Hell.
Except those who repent and believe (in the Oneness of Allaah and His Messenger Muhammad), and work righteousness. Such will enter Paradise and they will not be wronged in aught”
[Maryam 19:59, 60] 
A number of scholars were of the view that the one who misses a single prayer and delays it until its time is over, with no excuse, is a kaafir. So what you have to do is to repent to Allaah from this great sin, and pray regularly on time, as well as doing a lot of naafil prayers, in the hope that Allaah will forgive you and accept your good deeds.

question: If we pray behind a Mushrik Imam who sacrifices for graveyards and calls the dead, is our prayer accepted?
title: If we pray behind a Mushrik Imam who sacrifices for graveyards and calls the dead, is our prayer accepted?
answer:
the general rule is that it is permissible to pray behind anyone whose prayer is valid for himself. This means that as long as he is Muslim and there isn’t anything apparent that nullifies his Islam, this means that his prayer is valid for himself and for those behind him. That is why Ibn Omer, may Allah be pleased with him used to pray behind Al Hajjaj Al Thaqafi who was a tyrant and killed one of the great companions and a number of Al Tabi’een, because he was a Muslim, though an evil one.
Therefore, if the Imam of this masjid is a Muslim and doesn’t nullify his Islam, you can pray behind him. But if he calls the saints and slaughters to their graves, this is major Shirk and you can’t pray behind him.
Having said that, it is important not to cross the line and refuse to pray behind individuals simply because we don’t know their Aqeedah. This is the doing of Al Khawarij. Pray behind anyone who claims to be Muslim until you have concrete evidence that he is not Muslim.

question: i did istikhara many times before marriage but i got divorce n before remarrying i did istikhara many times but again im in an abusive marriage.whats wrong with it.when prophet saw told by doing istikhara one wont fail then why my wedded life isnt normal?
title: i did istikhara many times before marriage but i got divorce n before remarrying i did istikhara many times but again im in an abusive marriage.whats wrong with it.when prophet saw told by doing istikhara one wont fail then why my wedded life isnt normal?
answer:
Istikhara is not for your whole life! It is for the marriage to go ahead with it or not! The decision was good to marry that particular person! However, what comes afterwards is your own fault whether you didn’t manage this relationship well or you didn’t base your choice on what pleases Allah. For example, a drunkard proposes to you and you pray istikhara and you go ahead and marry him! Istikhara was wrong in the first place to be performed!

question: Is it forbidden to pray nafl salah after maghrib? Also the awabeen prayer after maghrib is this authentic and if not then is it bida to pray after maghrib?
title: Is it forbidden to pray nafl salah after maghrib? Also the awabeen prayer after maghrib is this authentic and if not then is it bida to pray after maghrib?
answer:
No, nafil prayer is not forbidden at any time except after Fajr uptil the sun rises a little high, at noon for few minutes when the sun is overhead and after Asr. Awabeen prayer is duha prayer and there isn’t any such prayer after Maghreb as the hadeeth is not authentic.

question: Which part of the body should touch the ground first while going down into sujood: hands or knees?
title: Which part of the body should touch the ground first while going down into sujood: hands or knees?
answer:
Praise be to Allaah.
The scholars have differed as to how one should go down in sujood, whether one should go hands first or knees first. According to the Hanafis, Shaafa’is and one opinion narrated from Ahmad, the person who is praying should go down on his knees first, then on his hands. Al-Tirmidhi thought that this was the opinion of the majority of scholars, and said in his Sunan (2/57): “This is how it is done according to the majority of scholars: they think that a man should go down on his knees before he puts his hands down, and when he gets up he should raise his hands before his knees. Those who express this opinion take as evidence the hadeeth of Waa’il ibn Hajar, who said: “I saw the Messenger of Allaah (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him), when he did sujood, putting his knees down before his hands, and when he got up he raised his hands before his knees.” (Reported by Abu Dawood, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nisaa’i, Ibn Maajah and al-Daaraqutni (1/345). He said: The only one who narrated it was Yazeed ibn Haaroon from Shurayk. Nobody reported from ‘Aasim ibn Kulayb except Shurayk, and Shurayk is not qawiy (strong). Al-Bayhaqi said in al-Sunan (2/101): its isnaad is da’eef (weak). Al-Albaani classed it as da’eef in al-Mishkaat (898) and al-Irwa’ (2/75). Other scholars classed it as saheeh, such as Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allaah have mercy on him) in Zaad al-Ma’aad). Among those who thought that one should go down into sujood knees first were Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyah and his student Ibn al-Qayyim; contemporary scholars who favour this view include Shaykh ‘Abd al-‘Azeez ibn Baaz and Shaykh Muhammad ibn Saalih al-‘Uthaymeen.
Maalik, al-Awzaa’i and the scholars of hadeeth thought that one should go into sujood hands first, based on the hadeeth of Abu Hurayrah (may Allaah be pleased with him), who said: “The Messenger of Allaah (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said, ‘When any one of you prostrates, let him not go down as the camel does; let hi

question: I wanted to know how I can  pray zuhar prayers when I am in the exam centre. The exam centre is really small. so i wont have a separate vacant place to pray.And by the time i finish my exam and reach home it will already be asar time.  I dont know in which direction i will be seated… Is it still ok to pray with ishara/ imagine each step aand recite duas in my heart?  I am really scared about this exam..and have written it a couple of times and wasnt able to get through, Could you advice dua or namaaz, which will help me make dua to clear the exam. .
title: I wanted to know how I can  pray zuhar prayers when I am in the exam centre. The exam centre is really small. so i wont have a separate vacant place to pray.And by the time i finish my exam and reach home it will already be asar time.  I dont know in which direction i will be seated… Is it still ok to pray with ishara/ imagine each step aand recite duas in my heart?  I am really scared about this exam..and have written it a couple of times and wasnt able to get through, Could you advice dua or namaaz, which will help me make dua to clear the exam. .
answer:
It is not allowed to pray sitting, you must pray the fardh standing up. You can ask for permission to pray, if it’s not given you can pray after the exam if the time for the prayer did not expire before reaching your home. question: Actually I am a medical student and we have to give our test in wards so we have to sit with the patients. We don’t get any break. My question is can we pray in naqab if there are non mahram around us? And if we have bench available only and the floor isn’t clean, then can we sit and pray on the bench?!
title: Actually I am a medical student and we have to give our test in wards so we have to sit with the patients. We don’t get any break. My question is can we pray in naqab if there are non mahram around us? And if we have bench available only and the floor isn’t clean, then can we sit and pray on the bench?!
answer:
You should find a place to pray that is secluded, and mustn’t pray in public unless as a necessity. In this case, you can keep your face covered and you can pray on any ground whether clean or dirty as long as there is no najasah or impurity that prevents prayer.

question: Recently I was in a shopping mall in the UK and I had just realised I had just about half an hour until Asr adhan and hadn’t done my dhur salah yet. My mother and aunty had gone off somewhere and I was alone with my freind and we are young. I could not tell the direction to pray in as the sun was blocked. What should I have done? I prayed after, is it accepted?
title: Recently I was in a shopping mall in the UK and I had just realised I had just about half an hour until Asr adhan and hadn’t done my dhur salah yet. My mother and aunty had gone off somewhere and I was alone with my freind and we are young. I could not tell the direction to pray in as the sun was blocked. What should I have done? I prayed after, is it accepted?
answer:
No, it is not! You should have asked any Muslim about the direction or any non muslim about the direction of east or north. Even if you couldn’t find anyone to tell you, you should have made your best to face what you think is the qibla and prayed before the time was over.

question: Description of the Prophet’s prayer
title: Description of the Prophet’s prayer
answer:
What is Description of the Prophet’s prayer ?.


 Praise be to Allah1 – Facing the direction of the Ka’bah
1-                 When you stand up to pray, face the direction of the Ka’bah wherever you are, in both fard (obligatory) and naafil (supererogatory) prayers. This is one of the pillars of prayer, without which prayer is not valid.
2-                 The obligation of facing the direction of prayer does not apply to one who is engaged in warfare, when he prays the fear prayer (salaat al-khawf) or is engaged in heavy fighting. It also does not apply to those who are unable to do it, such as one who is sick, or one who is traveling on a ship, in a car or on a plane, if they fear that the time of the prayer will elapse (before they reach a place where they can find the correct direction). And it does not apply to one who is praying a naafil prayer or witr prayer whilst riding on a riding-animal etc., but it is mustahabb for him to face the qiblah if he is able to do so when pronouncing the takbeer of ihraam (at the beginning of the prayer), then he may face whatever direction he is facing.
3-                 Everyone who can see the Ka’bah must face it; those who cannot see it must face its direction.
Ruling on not facing the Ka’bah in prayer by mistake:
4-                 If a person prays not facing the qiblah, because of clouds [preventing him from working out the direction from the position of the sun] or some other reason, after he did his best to work out the right direction, his prayer is valid and he does not have to repeat it.
5-                 If someone whom he trusts comes – whilst he is praying – and tells him of the right direction, then he must hasten to turn that way, and his prayer is valid.
2 – Qiyaam (standing in prayer)
6-                 It is obligatory to pray standing. This is a pillar (essential part of prayer), except for the one who is praying the fear prayer or at times of intense fighting, when it is permitted to pray whilst

question: I am aware that we cannot pray the deliberately missed salah. But my question is – I live and work in a non muslim country(India) and I can not pray Asr as my employer would not accept me removing time from work hours for my personal work ,though I pray dhuhr in lunch break. I needed to know, is this considered deliberately missing salah?
title: I am aware that we cannot pray the deliberately missed salah. But my question is – I live and work in a non muslim country(India) and I can not pray Asr as my employer would not accept me removing time from work hours for my personal work ,though I pray dhuhr in lunch break. I needed to know, is this considered deliberately missing salah?
answer:
It is a major sin to miss salah for no valid reason. You can always go to the toilet and then pray for five minutes and go back to work. You don’t have to go to a special place or to the masjid if work doesn’t permit you.
If your current employer does not allow you to do even this, then change your job!

question: When finishing the prayer, should we say one tasleem or two?
title: When finishing the prayer, should we say one tasleem or two?
answer:
Praise be to Allaah.  Shaykh Ibn Baaz (may Allaah have mercy on him) said:
The majority of scholars said that one tasleem is sufficient because evidence to that effect was narrated in some ahaadeeth. But a group of scholars stated that there have to be two tasleems because of the soundness of the ahaadeeth from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) which prove that, and because he said: “Pray as you have seen me praying.” (Narrated by al-Bukhaari in his Saheeh). This view is the one which is correct.
The view that one tasleem is sufficient is da’eef (weak) because of the weakness of the ahaadeeth that were narrated concerning that, and because there is ambiguity in these reports. If they are saheeh then they are shaadhdh (odd), because they go against reports which are more saheeh, more sound and more clear. But whoever does that – i.e., says one tasleem – out of ignorance or believing that the ahaadeeth concerning that are saheeh, his prayer is still valid. And Allaah is the Source of strength.

Tuhfat al-Ikhwaan, p. 112
www.islamqa.com

question: If eclipse (solar & moon) happen, do we have to offer As-Salat, if yes, do we have to pray in home or in Masjid, and how many Rakat have to offer?
title: If eclipse (solar & moon) happen, do we have to offer As-Salat, if yes, do we have to pray in home or in Masjid, and how many Rakat have to offer?
answer:
It is Fard Kifaya, which means if a group of Muslims do it, this is sufficient for all but if not one does it, they are all sinful. It is composed of 2 units like Fajr prayer but instead of having one Ruku in every unit, there are 2 ruku. This means that the prayer is composed of 2 units with 4 ruku and 4 sajdah (prostrations)
And Allah knows best

How can I distill this in her mind and heart, so she realises the importance of islam in this life. also can you tell me what is the minimum she needs to do, to complete her fard prayers.
title: I have been trying to teach my mother how to pray, but it is very difficult as she has no form of education islamic tr otherwise. She can not remember many things and she gets mixed up with what i try to teach.And she doesnt undastand and has no fear when i tell her about the grave or hereafter or hell. How can I distill this in her mind and heart, so she realises the importance of islam in this life. also can you tell me what is the minimum she needs to do, to complete her fard prayers.
answer:
Try to have her pray with you for a few weeks. This way, she will learn by example. She must recite the Fatiha in every rak’ah and say the supplications in the Ruku and sujood once at least. If she is unable to recite the Fatiha, she can say subhana Allah wal hamdu li Allah wa Allahu Akbar wa li ilaha illa Allah, throughout the prayer. 
And Allah knows best

question: Please let me know that how many riqaa i should pray at home for quyam, and shall i pray with the t.v from live through makkah please let me know . because i am new muslim.
title: Please let me know that how many riqaa i should pray at home for quyam, and shall i pray with the t.v from live through makkah please let me know . because i am new muslim.
answer:
Night prayers are any prayer you pray after Isha prayer and before the Athan of Fajr (the break of dawn).
This prayer is always prayed in odd total. The best is to pray 11 Rak’ah. 
The minimum you can pray is one rak’ah but there is no ceiling for the maximum number you can pray, providing that you pray odd number; i.e. 2+2+2 …… and when you want to conclude your prayers, you should pray wither 3 or one rak’ah so that the total would be odd number.
It is not permissible to pray with the TV as this is not congregational prayer. You have to be with them for your prayer to be valid as congregation
And Allah knows best

question: I want to know, which salaah is fadr, is it Dhuhr or Jummah salaah?
title: I want to know, which salaah is fadr, is it Dhuhr or Jummah salaah?
answer:
Both are considered to be Fard.
But when a person is residing and has not legitimate excuse to skip Friday, he obliged to pray it. 
If he has a legitimate excuse – as in the case of illness- in this case, Thuhur becomes Fard.

question: During the Tarawih prayer can we keep in our hands a copy of the Translation of the Meanings of the Quran and follow so we can understand what is the Imam saying?
title: During the Tarawih prayer can we keep in our hands a copy of the Translation of the Meanings of the Quran and follow so we can understand what is the Imam saying?
answer:
No, as this is reading something other than the Quran. It is permissible but not recommended to hold the Arabic Quran and to follow behind the Imam. Reading the translation would be like reading other books as this is not the word of Allah but a translation that might be right and it might be wrong.
And Allah knows best

question: Sheikh, i  saw some people here after they pray Fard they change their places for pray Sunnah(yanii thei dont pray in the same place where they pray Fard)…is this recommendable?
title: Sheikh, i  saw some people here after they pray Fard they change their places for pray Sunnah(yanii thei dont pray in the same place where they pray Fard)…is this recommendable?
answer:
Some scholars say that this is so that the ground would testify that a person prayed on it. So this way, there will be a number of spots testifying for you.
There is another hadeeth where the Prophet salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam has instructed us not to pray after the mandatory prayer except after talking or changing the spot.
Scholars say that this is especially after Friday prayer only. Others say that this is general.
However, if a person prays in the same spot, this is permissible. 
And Allah knows best

question: After the first tashahud can we raise the hands from sitting down (at Takbeer) or when we stand up? What is the most authentic opinion with regards to this.
title: After the first tashahud can we raise the hands from sitting down (at Takbeer) or when we stand up? What is the most authentic opinion with regards to this.
answer:
Some scholars say that you should raise your hands when you stand up as Sheikh Bin Bazz and Ibn Othaimeen say. Others, such as Sheikh AL Albani say you should do it while you are sitting down and before you stand up as this was reported by Ibn Omer.
I don’t have any solid proof on this issue but I do it when I stand up and I believe that both are acceptable, though the first is more practiced by Muslims. 
And Allah knows best

question: After i closed my prays with witr before i go to sleep, can i waik in the night to pray qiam al layl?
title: After i closed my prays with witr before i go to sleep, can i waik in the night to pray qiam al layl?
answer:
It is recommended that a person end his night prayers with Witr, providing he knows he can pray it before Fajr. But if a person fears that he might over sleep until the Athan, it is permissible for him or her to pray Witr before going to bed and then if she wakes up before Fajr, she can pray as many Rak’ah as she wishes providing that she doesn’t perform Witr again.
And Allah knows best

question: It is from the sunnah to pray our night prayer while sitting on chair, even though we don’t have any health problems? The Prophet (sallallahu aleihi wa sallam) did this?
title: It is from the sunnah to pray our night prayer while sitting on chair, even though we don’t have any health problems? The Prophet (sallallahu aleihi wa sallam) did this?
answer:
No, it is not from the Sunnah. It will decrease the reward of an individual by half if he doesn’t have a legitimate reason.
The Prophet salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam never prayed sitting down until he grew old and ill. While he was healthy, he would stand until his feet got swollen

question: A sister dont have a masjed in her town ,can she make her salah for aid in her home? Or its not recommadable?
title: A sister dont have a masjed in her town ,can she make her salah for aid in her home? Or its not recommadable?
answer:
Originally, Eid prayer is not recommended in Masjids unless there is rain or something that prevents Muslims from praying it in the open. 
It must be in congregation and can not be prayed alone or with a group in a house.

I have to leave my house NO LATER than 6 AM to get to work on time due to the fact I have to travel through 20 miles of some of the worst traffic in the United States. However, the Fajr adhan is at the moment at 06:04. If I wait and pray (at home) right after the adhan the fastest I can be on the roadis 06:15 and that would make me late. I would really appreciate some advice on this!

question: In our country imam dose not recites tahjud prayers in congregation.how many rakahs are there in tahjud.in our country imam normally recites 20 rakahs but i normally quit after 10 rakahs and then i perform 1 rakah of witr indiviually because they perform witr in a way which is not in accordance with the saying of the prophet(peace be upon him).is my act correct?

You should pray with the Imam until he concludes all his 23 rak’ah. If he prays the last 3 rak’ah like Maghrib prayer, pray with him but when you offers salam, you should stand up and finish your 4th rak’ah. Later on, you can offer witr in your home or in the masjid.

I had a software loaded in my mobile and it calculates the timings as per Saudi system.During these paryers there is always a difference on at least one hour i.e ZUHRis at 2 pm and ASR is at 5pm. Now in situations like this is it necessary to pray alone at home at their early stated timings or pray with Jamaat at late timings. title: I am always in a dilemma when I go for vacation. The timings of prayers especially ZUHR and ASR is delayed by at least one hour. I had a software loaded in my mobile and it calculates the timings as per Saudi system.During these paryers there is always a difference on at least one hour i.e ZUHRis at 2 pm and ASR is at 5pm. Now in situations like this is it necessary to pray alone at home at their early stated timings or pray with Jamaat at late timings. Only a few Masjids follow the prayers at their early stated timings.
answer:
Islamically, you are not allowed to abandon prayers with the congregation on the account that your clock’s calculation says differently. You have to try and find the time of prayers through observing the sun. if this is not possible, you have to pray with the Muslims.

question: I would like to know if when one is following the imam in a congregational prayer one has to recite fatiha? and if yes what if you dont finish the fatiha and the imam goes for ruku.
title: I would like to know if when one is following the imam in a congregational prayer one has to recite fatiha? and if yes what if you dont finish the fatiha and the imam goes for ruku.

It is an issue of dispute among scholars whether it is mandatory to recite the Fatiha after the Imam in loud prayers or not.

question: Can  you tell me please the Arkan of prayer?
title: Can  you tell me please the Arkan of prayer?
answer:
The pillars of prayer, of which there are fourteen, as follows: 
(i) Standing during obligatory prayers if one is able to do so
(ii) The opening takbeer (saying “Allaahu akbar”)
(iii) Reciting al-Faatihah
(iv) Rukoo’ (bowing), the least of which means bending so that the hands can touch the knees, but the most complete form means making the back level and the head parallel with it.
(v) Rising from bowing
(vi) Standing up straight
(vii) Sujood (prostration), the most perfect form of which is placing the forehead, nose, palms, knees and toes firmly on the ground, and the least of which is placing a part of each of these on the ground.
(viii) Rising from prostration
(ix) Sitting between the two prostrations. However one sits is good enough, but the Sunnah is to sit muftarishan, which means sitting on the left foot and holding the right foot upright with the toes pointing towards the qiblah.
(x) Being at ease in each of these physical pillars
(xi) The final tashahhud
(xii) Sitting to recite the final tashahhud and the two salaams
(xiii) The two salaams. This means saying twice, “al-salaamu ‘alaykum wa rahmat-Allaah (Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allaah).” In naafil prayers it is sufficient to say one salaam; the same also applies to the funeral prayer.
(xiv) Doing the pillars in the order mentioned here. If a person deliberately prostrates before bowing, for example, the prayer is invalidated; if he does that by mistake, he has to go back and bow, and then prostrate.

question: I missed my Asar salah to pray on time & my fellow colleague argue with me when I wanted to pray before magrib and said it is “Kaza” prayer of Asar what you are offering, Pls advice me!
title: I missed my Asar salah to pray on time & my fellow colleague argue with me when I wanted to pray before magrib and said it is “Kaza” prayer of Asar what you are offering, Pls advice me!
answer:
There are two times for praying Asr prayer.
The normal time begins from when the shade of an erected object is equivalent to its length. The evidence for this is the hadeeth of Jibreel, peace be upon him when he prayed with the Prophet salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam telling him the times of prayers.
The second time is for emergencies and this is extended up to just before sunset. The evidence for this is the hadeeth were the Prophet salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam says that whoever prays one Rak’ah before sunset, he has prayed Asr.
As for deliberately delaying the prayer till the time is out, there is no Kad’ah for that and it wouldn’t be accepted if a person delays it for no legitimate reason. He is sinful and this is a major sin.

question: What should I do if I forget to do sujud or ruku and later I realise that before completing the prayers?
title: What should I do if I forget to do sujud or ruku and later I realise that before completing the prayers?
answer:
If you forgot something that is a pillar of prayer such as Al Fatiha, the bowing, the prostration etc, you have to cancel that Rak’ah and consider what was after it in its place and offer another Rak’ah in its place. After you finish your prayer, you have to offer two prostrations and another salam.

question: I would like to know some information on ishtikara salah. Why is it performed and how is it performed.Assalam alaikum. How do I pray salat al istikhara, at what times , and are there special dua that I can read for different cicumstances?
title: I would like to know some information on ishtikara salah. Why is it performed and how is it performed.Assalam alaikum. How do I pray salat al istikhara, at what times , and are there special dua that I can read for different cicumstances?
answer:
Praise be to Allaah.
The description of Salaat al-Istikhaarah was reported by Jaabir ibn ‘Abd-Allaah al-Salami (may Allaah be pleased with him) who said:
“The Messenger of Allaah (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) used to teach his companions to make istikhaarah in all things, just as he used to teach them soorahs from the Qur’aan. He said: ‘If any one of you is concerned about a decision he has to make, then let him pray two rak’ahs of non-obligatory prayer, then say: Allaahumma inni astakheeruka bi ‘ilmika wa astaqdiruka bi qudratika wa as’aluka min fadlika, fa innaka taqdiru wa laa aqdir, wa ta’lamu wa laa a’lam, wa anta ‘allaam al-ghuyoob. Allaahumma fa in kunta ta’lamu haadha’l-amra (then the matter should be mentioned by name) khayran li fi ‘aajil amri wa aajilihi (or: fi deeni wa ma’aashi wa ‘aaqibati amri) faqdurhu li wa yassirhu li thumma baarik li fihi. Allaahumma wa in kunta ta’lamu annahu sharrun li fi deeni wa ma’aashi wa ‘aaqibati amri (or: fi ‘aajili amri wa aajilihi) fasrifni ‘anhu [wasrafhu ‘anni] waqdur li al-khayr haythu kaana thumma radini bihi (O Allaah, I seek Your guidance [in making a choice] by virtue of Your knowledge, and I seek ability by virtue of Your power, and I ask You of Your great bounty. You have power, I have none. And You know, I know not. You are the Knower of hidden things. O Allaah, if in Your knowledge, this matter (then it should be mentioned by name) is good for me both in this world and in the Hereafter (or: in my religion, my livelihood and my affairs), then ordain it for me, make it easy for me, and bless it for me. And if in Your knowledge it is bad for me and for my religion, my livelihood and my affairs (or: for me both in this world and the next), then turn me away from it, [and turn it away from me], and ordain for me the good wherever it may be and make me pleased with it.”
(Reported by al-Bukhaari, 6841; similar reports are also recorded by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nisaa’i, Abu Dawood, Ibn Maajah and Ahm

question: I have been doing Salat Al IStikhara for the past 2 days. For the first day, I don’t remember the dream, 2nd night; I saw the person in the dream, but still am not sure what it was all about. What do I do? It is actually about a boy, whom I have come across and have started to have a liking towards him. I haven’t met him yet, thinking that once the Istikhara is positive, I would meet him. Can you please give me some duas, on how he should show interest, rather than me chasing him?
title: I have been doing Salat Al IStikhara for the past 2 days. For the first day, I don’t remember the dream, 2nd night; I saw the person in the dream, but still am not sure what it was all about. What do I do? It is actually about a boy, whom I have come across and have started to have a liking towards him. I haven’t met him yet, thinking that once the Istikhara is positive, I would meet him. Can you please give me some duas, on how he should show interest, rather than me chasing him?
answer:
The purpose of Istikhara is asking Allah to choose for you something that you are about to do. Dreams don’t have anything to do with it.
As for your condition, you shouldn’t be attached to the idea of getting married to this brother as he didn’t propose and you can’t sell yourself cheap by hinting to him through a third party. You have to forget this brother and don’t allow Satan to get control over you. The brother is not interested in you and may have no intention to get married soon.
Therefore, focus on what would increase you Iman rather than what would bother your thinking without any result.

question: I had performed istikhara and now the things between me and my husband are not well.What is exactly the role of istikhara in our life’s ?Istikhara is seeking Allah’s choice in a particular issue. If things worked out well, this means that the marriage is a good thing for both the man and wife. If things later on came to be bad between them, this is due to their own fault and not that the marriage was bad. Otherwise, we would all do istkhara before going to university and before accepting a job etc and demand that nothing wrong happens.
title: I had performed istikhara and now the things between me and my husband are not well.What is exactly the role of istikhara in our life’s ?Istikhara is seeking Allah’s choice in a particular issue. title: How many miles do I have to travel in order to for me to be considered as a traveler? or is it traveling one place to another i.e different city to another city despite the distance is not far apart?

title: In terms of shortening or combining the salah whilst traveling, How many rakats do I need to shorten by?When salahs are combined and shorten due to travelling when do i perform the combined salah?

You pray thuhur 2 rak’ah and then you offer salam. After that you pray Asr prayer 2 rak’ah and after that you offer salam.
You can do all of that depending on your convenience. The same goes for Maghrib and Isha, however maghrib is not shortened while Isha is. There are two types of combining, one is to pray it at the time of the first prayer and the second is to pray it on the time of the second prayer, whether in the beginning, middle or end.

question: Please tell me that in the Salah, how much distance should be remain between our legs when we stand for the Salah (in standing position)?
title: Please tell me that in the Salah, how much distance should be remain between our legs when we stand for the Salah (in standing position)?
answer:
Arranging the rows during prayer
Many people do not know that it is from the sunnah to stand feet to feet and so during a jamaa’h, they leave a small gap in between. To what extent are we obliged to try and fill the gap by spreading our feet further apart? If the line is not straight, do we align ouselves to the person on our right, or the one on the left?.
Praise be to Allaah.
It is obligatory for the Muslims to make their rows straight and compact and to close the gaps between them. That is done by standing shoulder-to-shoulder and foot-to-foot.
It was narrated from Anas ibn Maalik that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “Make your rows straight for I can see you behind my back.”
Narrated by al-Bukhaari, 686; Muslim, 425.
It was narrated from ‘Abd-Allaah ibn ‘Umar that the Messenger of Allaah (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “Make your rows straight, stand shoulder to shoulder and close the gaps, and do not resist your brothers’ hands. Do not leave any gaps for the Shaytaan. Whoever complete a row, Allaah will reward him, and whoever breaksa row, Allaah will forsake him.
Abu Dawood said: What is meant by “Do not resist your brothers’ hands” is that a man should be easy-going if his brother pushes him forwards or backwards to make the row straight. (‘Awn al-Ma’bood).
Narrated by Abu Dawood, 666; al-Nasaa’i, 819. Classed as saheeh by al-Albaani in Saheeh Abi Dawood, 620.
It was narrated that al-Nu’maan ibn Basheer said:
“The Messenger of Allaah (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) turned to face the people and said, ‘Straighten your rows,’ three times, ‘for by Allaah either you straighten your rows or Allaah will create division among your hearts.’ And I saw men standing shoulder to shoulder, knee to knee, ankle to ankle.”
Narrated by Abu Dawood, 662; classed as saheeh by al-Albaani in Saheeh Abi Dawood, 616.

question: Do you think Umer ibn Khattab (RA) did invented a bidaa’ making people pray Taraweeh Salat with Jamaa’t & 20 Rakaa’t? Because Abu Bakar (RA) & Holy Prophet (SAWW) never did that?
title: Do you think Umer ibn Khattab (RA) did invented a bidaa’ making people pray Taraweeh Salat with Jamaa’t & 20 Rakaa’t? Because Abu Bakar (RA) & Holy Prophet (SAWW) never did that?

Omer, may Allah be pleased with him didn’t invent or innovate. It was the Prophet salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam the first to pray Taraweeh for 4 nights and the companions would pray behind them. question: Please can you enlighten me on how to observe missed salat given the fact that there is another congregational prayer going on. For example if i miss salatul magrib and by the time i want to observe this salat ,salatul ishai is already been said. Now should i join them and pray slatul ishai after which i pray my salatul magreb, or should i pray salatul magreb thereby missing the congregational praying of salatul ishai?
title: Please can you enlighten me on how to observe missed salat given the fact that there is another congregational prayer going on. For example if i miss salatul magrib and by the time i want to observe this salat ,salatul ishai is already been said. Now should i join them and pray slatul ishai after which i pray my salatul magreb, or should i pray salatul magreb thereby missing the congregational praying of salatul ishai?
answer:
If the prayer is ongoing you should pray isha with the congragation and then pray your magreb. If the prayer is not ongoing you should pray magreb. If you missed magreb prayer for a reason that is not legitimate, you should not make it up as it wouldn’t be accepted.

title: Due to constant busy schedule and demand meetings- family and work front, I miss my prayers most of the times. I feel extremely guilty and I make-up for them but I feel from inside that I am sinning. Can you advise me on my situation?

question: My aunt has fractured her left leg and in severe pain.She has severe bone osteoporosis. She is also having incontinence of urine that need her to wear a pamper all the time. How does she perform her 5 obligatory prayers?
title: My aunt has fractured her left leg and in severe pain.She has severe bone osteoporosis. She is also having incontinence of urine that need her to wear a pamper all the time. How does she perform her 5 obligatory prayers?
answer:
May Allah make it easy on your aunt. She has to pray on time and in clean body and clothes. These are two of the conditions of prayer. 
If she can remove the pampers and pray clean after washing, if she can make wudhu and if she can pray each prayer on time, she should do that. But if she is unable to pray clean due to her continuous urine problem, she can pray as she is. 
If she can’t perform wudhu because it is really too painful or due to her injuries, she should wash the areas she can and then perform wudhu on behalf of the rest. 
If she can’t pray on time due to fainting or because it is too hard for her to clean herself and perform wudhu 5 times a day, she can combine Thuhur with Asr and Maghrib with Isha.

question: A query regarding witr in Isha prayer.How should we pray witr?
title: A query regarding witr in Isha prayer.How should we pray witr?
answer:
Witr  means odd number.
The Sunnah is to offer witr in 3, 5, 7 or 9 rak’ah.
One rak’ah alone does the job. However, the best is to pray it as 3 rak’ah as the Prophet salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam used to do.
You can do this either by praying two rak’ah and then offering salam and after that praying one rak’ah or you can pray 3 rak’ah without sitting in the second rak’ah and then giving salam after the third rak’ah.

question: Which are the pillars of prayer?
title: Which are the pillars of prayer?
answer:
(i) Standing during obligatory prayers if one is able to do so
(ii)The opening takbeer (saying “Allaahu akbar”)
(iii)Reciting al-Faatihah
(iv)Rukoo’ (bowing), the least of which means bending so that the hands can touch the knees, but the most complete form means making the back level and the head parallel with it.
(v)Rising from bowing
(vi)Standing up straight
(vii)Sujood (prostration), the most perfect form of which is placing the forehead, nose, palms, knees and toes firmly on the ground, and the least of which is placing a part of each of these on the ground.
(viii)Rising from prostration
(ix) Sitting between the two prostrations. However one sits is good enough, but the Sunnah is to sit muftarishan, which means sitting on the left foot and holding the right foot upright with the toes pointing towards the qiblah.
(x)Being at ease in each of these physical pillars
(xi)The final tashahhud
(xii)Sitting to recite the final tashahhud and the two salaams
(xiii)The two salaams. This means saying twice, “al-salaamu ‘alaykum wa rahmat-Allaah (Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allaah).” In naafil prayers it is sufficient to say one salaam; the same also applies to the funeral prayer
(xiv)Doing the pillars in the order mentioned here. If a person deliberately prostrates before bowing, for example, the prayer is invalidated; if he does that by mistake, he has to go back and bow, and then prostrate.

question: Will the prayers of one who drinks alcohol not be accepted for forty days?
title: Will the prayers of one who drinks alcohol not be accepted for forty days?
answer:
Praise  be to Allaah.
Yes, there are many saheeh ahaadeeth concerning the punishment for one who drinks alcohol, which say that his prayers will not be accepted for forty days. This was narrated from ‘Amr ibn al-‘Aas, Ibn ‘Abbaas, Ibn ‘Umar and Ibn ‘Amr.
See al-Silsilah al-Saheehah, 709, 2039, 2695, 1854.
One of these ahaadeeth was narrated by Ibn Maajah (3377) from ‘Abd-Allaah ibn ‘Amr who said: The Messenger of Allaah (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “Whoever drinks alcohol and gets drunk, his prayer will not be accepted for forty days and if he dies he will go to Hell. But if he repents, Allaah will accept his repentance. If he again drinks alcohol and gets drunk, his prayer will not be accepted for forty days and if he dies he will go to Hell. But if he repents, Allaah will accept his repentance. If he again drinks alcohol and gets drunk, his prayer will not be accepted for forty days and if he dies he will go to Hell. But if he repents, Allaah will accept his repentance. If he commits (this sin) again, then Allaah pledges to make him drink the mud of khabaal on the Day of Resurrection.” They asked, “O Messenger of Allaah, what is the mud of khabaal?” He said, “The juices of the people of Hell.”
Classed as saheeh by al-Albaani in Saheeh Ibn Maajah.
The fact that his prayers are not accepted does not mean that they are not valid, or that he should give up praying, rather it means that he will not be rewarded for them.
So the benefit of praying will be that he will have discharged his duty and will not be punished for not doing it.
Abu ‘Abd-Allaah ibn Mandah said: The words “his prayer will not be accepted” mean that he will not be rewarded for his prayer for forty days, as a punishment for his drinking alcohol, just as they say that the one who speaks on Friday when the imam is delivering the khutbah should pray Jumu’ah but there is no Jumu’ah for him, meaning that he will not be given the reward for Jumu’ah as a punishment for his sin.

question: Up to how many days is the limit for travelling and connecting salah to be applicable on a person? example travelling away from home city for more then 7 days which means the new city i shall be visiting i will be there for 7 days before returning home.
title: Up to how many days is the limit for travelling and connecting salah to be applicable on a person? example travelling away from home city for more then 7 days which means the new city i shall be visiting i will be there for 7 days before returning home.

It is an issue of dispute among scholars. The most authentic opinion is that as long as a person is still travelling and have not settled yet, he has the option to shorten prayers providing that there is no masjid in his vicinity. Therefore, 7 days is not enough to settle down.

question: I am a working woman. I need to pray Zohar at my work place. My question is that if I start from my house in the morning by making wudu is it ok if I do full wudu except washing my feet for my Zohar prayer?
title: I am a working woman. I need to pray Zohar at my work place. My question is that if I start from my house in the morning by making wudu is it ok if I do full wudu except washing my feet for my Zohar prayer?
answer:
If you leave home after making wudhu and you remain in the state of wudhu until Thuhur time, you can pray it without making another wudhu.
But if you nullified your wudhu, you have to make a new one in order to pray and you have to wash your feet as it is part of the pillars of wudhu.

question: Can a Muslim sit (for example in a plane seat or in a car seat) and pray while traveling or is this kind of improvisation not allowed? Do prayers done in this way in the past during travels need to be made up for?
title: Can a Muslim sit (for example in a plane seat or in a car seat) and pray while traveling or is this kind of improvisation not allowed? Do prayers done in this way in the past during travels need to be made up for?
answer:
In mandatory prayers, it is a pillar that one prays standing up. If a person is unable to stand up, he can pray sitting down.
If a person is travelling, he is allowed to pray voluntary prayers while sitting down, even to the direction of other than the Ka’abah.
While in the car and in the city, this is not permissible.

question: When is salat-ul-‘Asr?
title: When is salat-ul-‘Asr?
answer:
The time of ‘Asr
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “The time for ‘Asr lasts until the sun turns yellow.”
We know that the time for ‘Asr begins when the time for Zuhr ends, i.e., when the length of an object’s shadow becomes equal to the length of the object itself. There are two times for the end of ‘Asr.
(1) The preferred time: this lasts from the beginning of the time for ‘Asr until the sun begins to turn yellow, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “The time for ‘Asr lasts until the sun turns yellow.” Defining this time by the clock varies according to the season.
(2) The time of necessity. This lasts from the time the sun turns yellow until sunset, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “Whoever catches up with one rak’ah of ‘Asr before the sun sets has caught up with ‘Asr.” (Narrated by al-Bukhaari, 579; Muslim, 608)
Question: what is meant by the time of necessity?
Necessity here refers to when a person is distracted from praying ‘Asr by some essential and unavoidable work, such as dressing wounds, and he is able to pray before the sun turns yellow but it is difficult, then he prays just before sunset. In this case he has prayed on time and has not sinned, because this is the time of necessity. If a person is forced to delay the prayer, there is no sin so long as he prays before the sun sets.

question: Outside of the month of Ramadan, is salat-tul – thajud prayed in congreation and how many raakaats are prayed – 2, 4, 6 0r 8 or more/ If it is not prayed in congregation and I pray it by myself is it allowed to recite it aloud like Fajr,and so on

answer:
Tahajjud is night prayer that is performed before Fajr and after sleeping.

question: After Asr salaah congregation, how much time is there to perform your salaah if you have missed it before the sun starts to go down. Is it permissible to worship when sun starts setting till it finishes its setting?
title: After Asr salaah congregation, how much time is there to perform your salaah if you have missed it before the sun starts to go down. Is it permissible to worship when sun starts setting till it finishes its setting?
answer:
The time of ‘Asr 
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “The time for ‘Asr lasts until the sun turns yellow.” 
We know that the time for ‘Asr begins when the time for Zuhr ends, i.e., when the length of an object’s shadow becomes equal to the length of the object itself. There are two times for the end of ‘Asr. 
(1) The preferred time: this lasts from the beginning of the time for ‘Asr until the sun begins to turn yellow, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “The time for ‘Asr lasts until the sun turns yellow.” Defining this time by the clock varies according to the season.
(2) The time of necessity. This lasts from the time the sun turns yellow until sunset, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “Whoever catches up with one rak’ah of ‘Asr before the sun sets has caught up with ‘Asr.” (Narrated by al-Bukhaari, 579; Muslim, 608) 
Question: what is meant by the time of necessity? 
Necessity here refers to when a person is distracted from praying ‘Asr by some essential and unavoidable work, such as dressing wounds, and he is able to pray before the sun turns yellow but it is difficult, then he prays just before sunset. In this case he has prayed on time and has not sinned, because this is the time of necessity. If a person is forced to delay the prayer, there is no sin so long as he prays before the sun sets.

question: When is it prescribed for a worshipper to do the prostration of forgetfulness?
title: When is it prescribed for a worshipper to do the prostration of forgetfulness?
answer:
Praise be to Allaah.
By the mercy of Allaah to His slaves, as one of the beauties of this perfect religion, Allaah has prescribed that His slaves may make up for shortcomings and mistakes that they make in their worship and cannot avoid completely, by performing supererogatory (naafil) acts of worship, praying for forgiveness and so on.
One of the things that Allaah has prescribed for His slaves to make up for shortcomings that may occur in their prayer is the prostration of forgetfulness, but it is only prescribed to make up for certain things; it does not make up for everything nor is it prescribed for everything.
Shaykh Ibn ‘Uthaymeen (may Allaah have mercy on him) was asked about the reasons for doing the prostration of forgetfulness, and he replied as follows:
The prostration of forgetfulness in prayer is generally prescribed for three reasons:
1- Doing something extra
2- Omitting something
3- Being uncertain
Doing something extra: for example, doing an extra bow (rukoo’), prostration (sujood), standing or sitting.
Omitting something: such as omitting an essential part of the prayer, or omitting one of the obligatory parts of the prayer.
Being uncertain: such as when a person is not sure how many rak’ahs he has prayed, whether it was three or four, for example.
In the case of doing something extra, if a person adds something to his prayer – bowing, prostrating, standing or sitting – deliberately, then his prayer becomes invalid, because when he added it, that means that he did not do the prayer in the manner ordained by Allaah and His Messenger (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him). The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “Whoever does an action that is not part of this matter of ours (i.e., Islam), will have it rejected.” Narrated by Muslim, 1718.

question: Please tell me the right method of Witr Salah and right Du’a-e-Qunoot?Du’aa’ al-Qunoot in Witr prayer
title: Please tell me the right method of Witr Salah and right Du’a-e-Qunoot?Du’aa’ al-Qunoot in Witr prayer
answer:
Praise be to Allaah. 
Firstly: 
Du’a’ al-Qunoot is recited in the last rak’ah of Witr prayer, after bowing, but if one recites it before bowing it doesn’t matter. But reciting it after bowing is better. 
Shaykh al-Islam [Ibn Taymiyah] said in Majmoo’ al-Fataawa (23/100): 
With regard to qunoot: there are two extreme views and one middle (or moderate) view. Some say that qunoot should only be recited before bowing and some say that it should only be recited after bowing. The fuqaha’ among the scholars of hadeeth, such as Ahmad and others, say that both are allowed, because both are mentioned in the saheeh Sunnah, but they preferred reciting qunoot after bowing because this is mentioned more often. 
Raising the hands is mentioned in a saheeh report from ‘Umar (may Allaah be pleased with him), as was narrated by al-Bayhaqi in a report which he classed as saheeh (2/210). 
The worshipper should raise his hands to chest height and no more, because this du’aa’ is not a du’aa’ of supplication in which a person needs to raise his hands high. Rather it is a du’aa’ of hope in which a person holds out his palms towards heaven… The apparent meaning of the scholar’s words is that the worshipper should hold his hands close together like a beggar who asks someone else to give him something. 
It is better not to recite qunoot in witr all the time, rather it should be done sometimes, because there is no evidence that the Messenger of Allaah (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) did it all the time. But he taught al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali (may Allaah be pleased with him) a du’aa’ to recite in qunoot al-witr, as will be quoted below. 
Secondly: 
The du’aa’ of qunoot was narrated by Abu Dawood (1425), al-Tirmidhi (464), and al-Nasaa’i (1746) from al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali (may Allaah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allaah (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) taught me some words to say in qunoot al-witr: 
“Allaahumma ihdini feeman hadayta wa ‘aafini feeman ‘aafayta

question: I want to know if somebody was travelling back and front on not trips but for other important reasons and that person missed some prayers and doesn’t know exactly how much of prayers he missed, what does such a person do?
title: I want to know if somebody was travelling back and front on not trips but for other important reasons and that person missed some prayers and doesn’t know exactly how much of prayers he missed, what does such a person do?
answer:

question: After Asr salaah how long have you to perform your salaah if you have missed it before the sun starts to go down. Is it permissible to worship when the start of the sun goes down till it finishes going down?
title: After Asr salaah how long have you to perform your salaah if you have missed it before the sun starts to go down. Is it permissible to worship when the start of the sun goes down till it finishes going down?
answer:
The time of ‘Asr 
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “The time for ‘Asr lasts until the sun turns yellow.” 
We know that the time for ‘Asr begins when the time for Zuhr ends, i.e., when the length of an object’s shadow becomes equal to the length of the object itself. There are two times for the end of ‘Asr. 
(1) The preferred time: this lasts from the beginning of the time for ‘Asr until the sun begins to turn yellow, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “The time for ‘Asr lasts until the sun turns yellow.” Defining this time by the clock varies according to the season.
(2) The time of necessity. This lasts from the time the sun turns yellow until sunset, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “Whoever catches up with one rak’ah of ‘Asr before the sun sets has caught up with ‘Asr.” (Narrated by al-Bukhaari, 579; Muslim, 608) 
Question: what is meant by the time of necessity? 
Necessity here refers to when a person is distracted from praying ‘Asr by some essential and unavoidable work, such as dressing wounds, and he is able to pray before the sun turns yellow but it is difficult, then he prays just before sunset. In this case he has prayed on time and has not sinned, because this is the time of necessity. If a person is forced to delay the prayer, there is no sin so long as he prays before the sun sets.

question: I’ve noticed some of the brothers clasp their hands (just like they clasp their hands after saying initial Takbeer) in Salaah when they get up from rukuu. Is it part of Sunnah? Is there any hadith for this?
title: I’ve noticed some of the brothers clasp their hands (just like they clasp their hands after saying initial Takbeer) in Salaah when they get up from rukuu. Is it part of Sunnah? Is there any hadith for this?
answer:
Praise be to Allaah.
This is one of the issues on which the scholars (may Allaah have mercy on them) have differed. Some of them think that placing the right hand on the left forearm when standing up from rukoo’ is sunnah mustahabbah (preferable) because of the general meaning of the hadeeth of Sahl ibn Sa’d al-Saa’idi (may Allaah be pleased with him), who said: “The people were told that a man should place his right hand on his left forearm in prayer.” They said: the general meaning of the phrase “in prayer” makes it clear that when standing up from rukoo’, one should place one’s hands thus, because the qiyaam (standing) includes the standing both before rukoo’ and after, so a person should place his right hand on his left forearm in both qiyaams.
They said that during rukoo’, the hands should be on the knees, in sujood they should be on the ground, in juloos (sitting) they should be on the thighs, and in qiyaam (standing) they should be on the chest. This is where the hands should be during the qiyaam before rukoo’ and after. The attitude of humility and proper conduct before the Lord requires this in both qiyaams, and this position is the furthest away from fidgeting. Other scholars think that the right hand does not have to be placed on the left forearm after standing up from rukoo’, and their evidence is the fact that no specific report on this matter has been narrated, as well as the fact that the general meaning of qiyaam does not include standing up from rukoo’, because this is a straightening of the back, not a standing (qiyaam), so the person should let his hands drop to his sides.
Some scholars say that a person has the choice of placing his hands on his chest or not, because nothing clear has been reported in the Sunnah on this point. This is the opinion of Imaam Ahmad, may Allaah have mercy on him.
The first opinion is more likely to be correct, in sha Allaah, but in any case, either way is valid. Differences in such matters should not lead to

question: If somebody was traveling back and front on not trips, but for other important reasons and that person missed some prayers and doesn’t know exactly how much of prayers he missed what does such a person do?

question: I have learned that WITR prayer should preferably be prayed as the last prayer of the day. But if we pray Isha late, like 1:00 AM and fajr is due at 4:35am…and we are awake through the night, then at what time is it appropriate to do ISTIKHARA?
title: I have learned that WITR prayer should preferably be prayed as the last prayer of the day. But if we pray Isha late, like 1:00 AM and fajr is due at 4:35am…and we are awake through the night, then at what time is it appropriate to do ISTIKHARA?
answer:
The question is not clear.
First of all, it is not permissible to pray Isha prayer at 01:00 as this is way passed its time. Isha must be prayed before midnight which is half the time between Maghrib and Fajr.
Secondly, are you asking about witr or Istikhara? Istikhara has nothing to do with fajr or with Isha.
Finally, if you are asking about tahajjud, this has to be preceded by sleeping.

title: Today I woke up late and missed Fajr congregation, so I prayed at home The Fard prayer only during sunrise. is my prayer valid?
answer:
The Prophet salla Allahu alaihi wa sallam said that if a person oversleeps a prayer or forgets it, he should pray it as soon as he remembers it as there is no expiation for missing the prayer except this. From this hadeeth, scholars said that sleeping and forgetting a prayer can be expiated by praying immediately. 
They said that if a person deliberately postpones a prayer until the following prayer is due, he shouldn’t and he must not pray it as it wouldn’t be accepted from him because its time expired.

question: Sheikh, I want to ask if while praying and somebody finishes resiting suratul teen and at the end of the surah that person says sadha qallahu aladeem or balaa ya raab does that nullify that person’s praying?
title: Sheikh, I want to ask if while praying and somebody finishes resiting suratul teen and at the end of the surah that person says sadha qallahu aladeem or balaa ya raab does that nullify that person’s praying?
answer:
There is a weak hadeeth supporting the second sentence. Therefore, this doesn’t nullify the prayer. However, saying sadaqa Allahu alatheem, this is not part of the Quran and it is not part of the prescribed thikr. Therefore, it is most likely affects the prayer negatively and shouldn’t be said.

question: Is it ok if someone finishes praying ‘Asr around 1 hour before maghrib?
title: Is it ok if someone finishes praying ‘Asr around 1 hour before maghrib?
answer:
The time of ‘Asr
The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “The time for ‘Asr lasts until the sun turns yellow.”
We know that the time for ‘Asr begins when the time for Zuhr ends, i.e., when the length of an object’s shadow becomes equal to the length of the object itself. There are two times for the end of ‘Asr.
(1) The preferred time: this lasts from the beginning of the time for ‘Asr until the sun begins to turn yellow, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “The time for ‘Asr lasts until the sun turns yellow.” Defining this time by the clock varies according to the season.
(2) The time of necessity. This lasts from the time the sun turns yellow until sunset, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “Whoever catches up with one rak’ah of ‘Asr before the sun sets has caught up with ‘Asr.” (Narrated by al-Bukhaari, 579; Muslim, 608)
Question: what is meant by the time of necessity?
Necessity here refers to when a person is distracted from praying ‘Asr by some essential and unavoidable work, such as dressing wounds, and he is able to pray before the sun turns yellow but it is difficult, then he prays just before sunset. In this case he has prayed on time and has not sinned, because this is the time of necessity. If a person is forced to delay the prayer, there is no sin so long as he prays before the sun sets.

question: What is the ruling on a woman leading men in Jumu’ah and other prayers?
title: What is the ruling on a woman leading men in Jumu’ah and other prayers?
answer:
Praise be to Allaah.
Firstly:
Allaah has singled out men for some virtues and rulings, and He has singled out women for other virtues and rulings. It is not permissible for any man to wish for that which has been granted to women only, nor is it permissible for any woman to wish for that which has been granted to men. This kind of wishing is tantamount to objecting to the laws and rulings of Allaah.
Allaah says (interpretation of the meaning):
“And wish not for the things in which Allaah has made some of you to excel others. For men there is reward for what they have earned, (and likewise) for women there is reward for what they have earned, and ask Allaah of His Bounty. Surely, Allaah is Ever All‑Knower of everything”
[al-Nisa’ 4:32]
al-Sa’di (may Allaah have mercy on him) said:
Allaah forbids the believers to wish for that with which Allaah has favoured others, whether that is in things that are possible or things that are impossible. Women should not wish for the things that have been bestowed uniquely upon men, by which Allaah has favoured them over women, and no poor person or person who has shortcomings should merely wish for the position of one who is rich or perfect, because this is the essence of destructive envy (hasad)… and because that implies displeasure with the decree of Allaah. End quote.
One of the things for which Allaah has singled out men is that the acts of worship which require physical strength, such as jihad, or require a position of leadership such as leading the prayers, etc., are only for men, and women have nothing to do with them.
This is indicated by a great deal of evidence, such as the following:
1 – Allaah says (interpretation of the meaning):
“Men are the protectors and maintainers of women, because Allaah has made one of them to excel the other, and because they spend (to support them) from their means”
[al-Nisa’ 4:34]

question: Sheikh, if i make just one sujjud in a raka(due to long duas,i often am not sure wether i make one or two sujjuds,but i think morelikely that i made 2)or remember this(that i made just one sujud)only after the first tashahud then what should i do?Should i make sujud al sahu before the salam ?is it possible to make sujud al sahu before salam if one doubts he made something or not?
title: Sheikh, if i make just one sujjud in a raka(due to long duas,i often am not sure wether i make one or two sujjuds,but i think morelikely that i made 2)or remember this(that i made just one sujud)only after the first tashahud then what should i do?Should i make sujud al sahu before the salam ?is it possible to make sujud al sahu before salam if one doubts he made something or not?
answer:
In your situation, if you have most likely done your second sujood but you are not 100% sure, you should offer the forgetfulness prostrations after the salam and then offer another salam.

question: I am a young new Muslim studying. Where I am living is quiet far from the masjid. I am finding to attend all five prayers and spend time with my wife and study very strenuous.
